children: Air France-KLM's third-quarter figures show that the Franco-Dutch carrier group has managed to keep costs under control despite a growing fuel bill, RBC Capital Markets analyst Ruairi Cullinane writes in a research note. The group expects a roughly 1% increase this year in unit costs, a key measure of how much it costs an airline to fly a unit of capacity over a specific distance. Third-quarter net profit rose to 908 million euros from 730 million euros a year earlier. Adjusted operating profit--closely watched by investors--increased to 1.35 billion euros from 1.22 billion euros, above company-compiled consensus of 1.08 billion euros. Air France-KLM shares trade 13% higher at 12.78 euros. (mauro.orru@wsj.com)
